speakers.name: Zach Fadem (labelled Zach Ogden, for Andrew Charles)

exchanges.question: Does the lift from bringing LTOs back from the pantry (e.g. Chicken al Pastor) still build each time? Are there changes in value perception, and is the industry underpricing issue reflected?
exchanges.answer: Chipotle Honey Chicken performed better the second time, as do many LTOs, though there is a point of diminishing returns (perhaps the fifth or sixth time). Innovation and menu work is 4x what it was a couple of years ago. The brand tracker showed solid progress on value perception across all income groups and age cohorts, and affordability scores were better in Q2 than in probably the past couple of years; value is also convenience, execution and innovation, including the high-protein menu.

exchanges.question: Pushback is that Chipotle is doing and spending a lot for 1%-2% comps; where does confidence in momentum into 2027 come from, given tough comparisons and a recent slowdown, with guidance raised to low single digits?
exchanges.answer: Q2 transaction growth was early days of Recipe for Growth, especially menu innovation. Early proof points in guest satisfaction, food quality and operational consistency show it is on track, and additional drivers (menu innovation, deeper rewards engagement, stronger brand communication, group occasions) are showing green shoots and will build through H2 2026 and into 2027. New digital and brand leaders have not yet had their ideas shown; no quantified evidence given.

exchanges.question: More color on the low-single-digit positive comp guide, including Q3 and the recent softening and its cadence.
exchanges.answer: Q2 traffic improved through the quarter and momentum continued into the first half of July, then softened by about 200 basis points in the second half of July, around the industry Cyclospora issue. Q3 is the toughest lap and comps are expected around plus 1%, assuming the roughly 200 basis point impact continues. Boatwright: Chipotle is not involved in the Cyclospora conversation (affected on sales only); the implicated products are not on the menu and lettuces are sourced in California.

exchanges.question: Has the incremental capex and sales uplift from the restaurant remodel/refresh program (about 1,000-1,500 stores) been sized, and have you considered partners in other international markets rather than owning and operating?
exchanges.answer: Chipotle has never done an aesthetic remodel; this year it is stage-gating a refresh program at several locations, at roughly $100,000-$300,000 per restaurant, to test returns, with nothing to report yet. For international, Alshaya (Middle East), Alsea (Latin America) and SPC (Southeast Asia) are partner-operated or JV, built slowly; Western Europe remains owned and operated and the rest of the world partner-operated.

exchanges.question: Digital sales grew 18% including unit growth; was there a catalyst that unlocked this, and is it linked to loyalty and payment at the register?
exchanges.answer: It is all linked. Last year's Summer of Extras showed where Chipotle can win in digital, informing the rewards relaunch a couple of months ago (less app friction, more flexible earning and redemption); this year's Summer of Extras and an emerging trend add to it. Arlie Sisson is taking a holistic approach to digital and there is more work to do.

exchanges.question: Will HEAP labor efficiency be reinvested into labor on the production line, and could it drive traffic and customer satisfaction?
exchanges.answer: Yes. HEAP gives about two to four hours of efficiency depending on volume, left in the restaurant to get prep done in the morning and deploy labor on the line during peak, which shows up in transactions, Max 15 throughput, total sales and better taste scores. HEAP will be in 2,000 restaurants by year-end and hopes to cover the whole portfolio sometime in 2027; all new restaurants come with HEAP standard.

exchanges.question: Why is 350 company-operated openings per year the right level versus the prior ceiling of 400, and what is the gating factor to accelerating beyond 350?
exchanges.answer: Given US white space and the ability to develop ready-now leaders, one restaurant per day is meaningful growth; beyond 350 there may be diminishing returns or risk to fracture the base, and the team is comfortable with 350. Incremental growth comes from company-owned Western Europe and partner-operated markets, which ramp quickly: the Middle East partnership with Alshaya began a couple of years ago and is already at 15 restaurants across three or four countries, with meaningful acceleration in 2027.

exchanges.question: With a new CMO, how will the brand be positioned, given the For Real campaign has gone stale; will value and ingredient quality be highlighted more?
exchanges.answer: For Real was extraordinary and served the company for many years; Fernando Machado's work is the next evolution rather than a 180 pivot. Expect more on fresh in-restaurant preparation, ingredients and the brand's opportunity to cultivate a better world, with creative ambition to break through. Value will be highlighted as extraordinary value from best ingredients, fresh, in abundance, at speed and an approachable price point, not price points or discounts.

exchanges.question: Is the Q3 comp guide of about 1% an underlying trend of about 3% less a sustained roughly 200 basis point Cyclospora headwind? And where is Max 15 throughput system-wide excluding HEAP?
exchanges.answer: Yes, the 1% guide (and expense guidance) assumes the impact continues through the rest of the quarter, and it is very difficult to predict how long it lasts. HEAP restaurants do two or three more entrees in Max 15; overall in-store is in the low 20 range, digital (almost 40% of sales) mid-teen, and combined low to mid-30s per restaurant per day.

exchanges.question: What is working and what could be better in promoting loyalty in restaurant, and do the in-store transactions without loyalty over-index to lower-income guests?
exchanges.answer: No, the non-loyalty 20% of in-store transactions are more broad-based and could see meaningful lift if enrolled. Today's process (phone, loyalty app, card) is clunky; in August a one-stop pay pilot will award rewards points on payment and allow enrollment, without relying on the restaurant team so throughput is not hurt. More work remains to educate consumers in restaurant.

exchanges.question: Are the new menu items coming in the months ahead center-of-the-plate or sides, and any more detail?
exchanges.answer: The expanded culinary team is working on real new news, not just pantry items: center-of-the-plate items, beverage, sides and desserts. Some big ideas have been stage-gated and could be on the calendar in the back half of 2026, but certainly in 2027. No specific items named.

exchanges.question: Update on Q2 and Q3-to-date trends by age and income, particularly the younger and lower-to-middle-income cohorts, and frequency differences.
exchanges.answer: Rymer: the younger and lower-income cohorts, previously most pressured, have improved the most, with broad-based trends from Q1 into Q2 driven by menu innovation (Honey Chicken, Cilantro Lime Sauce), promotions (Matchday BOGO) and rewards. Boatwright: highest year-over-year gains in wallet share last quarter since 2024, with share taken in each month of 2026 across all income cohorts and age groups. No Q3-to-date cohort data was given.

exchanges.question: How is the margin outlook beyond Q3, given last quarter's comment on the gap between pricing and inflation narrowing near year end?
exchanges.answer: The gap between price and inflation was widest in H1 (pricing around 1% versus inflation low to mid 3%) and is easing in H2 with the rolling pricing approach. In Q3, inflation is expected closer to 3% and pricing in the mid 2% range, and from Q4 forward the two should match.

exchanges.question: Did the World Cup create regional divergences or a benefit? And what has been learned from the rolling pricing approach that gives comfort to land at the high end of the 1%-2% range?
exchanges.answer: World Cup impact was very small: about 300 restaurants within roughly 10 miles of stadiums saw a 50 to 100 basis point comp benefit during the tournament, but the impact on the overall quarter was less than five basis points. Rolling market-by-market pricing measures resistance precisely and adjusts for inflation; the earlier dislocation was just timing and the approach will continue.

exchanges.question: How much do LTOs contribute to frequency uplift, and do high-protein LTOs attract new guests or existing guests?
exchanges.answer: Rymer: no LTO-specific figures, but Honey Chicken and Chicken al Pastor raise transactions, from most frequent guests coming more often and new guests; typically hundreds of basis points of transaction lift, mostly sustained through the promotion, with stickiness after; a multi-year AUV lever. Boatwright: protein LTOs bring in new customers and raise lifetime value; expect a couple more center-of-the-plate items in H2, sides innovation and a bigger push into beverage.
